newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal ends up on China rumor, commercial.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal ends up on China rumor, commercial.

text.p: Commercial buying amid a rumor China bought 100,000 to 150,000 tonnes of U.S. soymeal for January through March shipment boosted CBOT soymeal futures to a higher close, traders said.
"There were China rumors in meal and good commercial buying so there could be something to it," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.
Continental Grain bought 1,200 lots of soymeal with 600 lots purchased in the January contract, traders said. The key commercial also took a bullish stance in soymeal options, options traders said.
Position squaring was noted before the release Thursday of USDA's world and U.S. supply/demand reports and weekly export sales report.
"Soymeal has been down hard recently and was due for a bounce," a trader said.
Soyoil closed mostly lower on adjustment of the soymeal/soyoil spread after the gains in oil early this week and losses in soymeal.
Soymeal closed $2.00 to $4.10 per ton higher, with December up $3.60 at $231.60. Soyoil was 0.05 cent per lb lower to 0.05 up, with December up 0.05 at 23.00 cents.
